title: Fix all findings in debug/26_7_4_debug_3.md (severity-ordered)
scope: Fix all 22 findings (6 Medium, 16 Low) from the third code-review report, highest severity first. Verify existing functionality (backend unit tests, frontend build/lint) after each fix. Mark each fixed finding as done (checkbox) in debug/26_7_4_debug_3.md and debug/26_7_4_debug_3_zh.md. Write a Chinese bug-fix report when done.

stories.title: Uncaught LLM/stream errors abort SSE with no terminator and persist a blank turn
stories.description: backend/app/service/agent/agent.py (_llm_json call sites in agent_plan/should_continue, final_answer streaming loop) and backend/app/router/chat_rt.py stream(): wrap the final_answer generator consumption in an except that yields a translated error event + event: end/data: [DONE], and skip (or explicitly error-mark) _persist() when no answer content was collected.
acceptanceCriteria: stream() in chat_rt.py catches exceptions raised while iterating final_answer() and yields a well-formed SSE error event followed by a proper stream terminator instead of letting the exception propagate uncaught
When no answer content was collected due to an upstream failure, _persist() does not silently write a blank successful turn (either skipped or persisted with an explicit error marker)
backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py and backend/tests/test_chat_router.py still pass
A new test exercises the mid-stream LLM-failure path (simulating an exception from final_answer) and asserts the stream terminates cleanly without persisting a blank turn

stories.title: Final-answer prompt uses unbounded raw memory instead of _bounded_memory
stories.description: backend/app/service/agent/agent.py: the final answer prompt does json.dumps(memory, ...) on raw memory while should_continue uses _bounded_memory(memory). Also _bounded_memory never bounds list[dict] fields (rag_search/web_search results).
acceptanceCriteria: The final-answer prompt uses a bounded version of memory (same _bounded_memory used by should_continue, or an extended variant)
List-valued memory fields (e.g. web_search/rag_search results) are capped in count/size, not just str fields
backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py still passes

stories.title: Aggregate PDF rasterization memory is unbounded despite per-page pixel cap
stories.description: backend/app/service/core/deepdoc/parser/pdf_parser.py:976 - all pages are materialized into self.page_images simultaneously; MAX_PDF_PAGES x MAX_PAGE_RENDER_PIXELS can multiply to ~4.5GB. Enforce an aggregate budget or release page images incrementally.
acceptanceCriteria: An aggregate pixel/byte budget across all rendered pages is enforced (or page images are processed and released in a streaming fashion) so total held rasterized memory is bounded regardless of per-page MediaBox size
Existing PDF parsing tests (if any) and backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py / test_chat_router.py still pass
A normal, reasonably-sized PDF still parses correctly and produces the same output as before

stories.title: Corrupt/mislabeled PDF raises opaque AttributeError instead of failing cleanly
stories.description: backend/app/service/core/deepdoc/parser/pdf_parser.py __images__: self.page_images/self.page_chars are only set inside the try block; if pdfplumber.open() fails, the except swallows the error but later code (range(len(self.page_chars))) crashes with an unrelated AttributeError.
acceptanceCriteria: self.page_images and self.page_chars are initialized to [] before the try block
On a pdfplumber.open() failure, the function returns early or raises a clear, typed error instead of allowing a later AttributeError
A test uploading a corrupt/non-PDF file renamed to .pdf results in a clean failed status via the router's existing exception handling, not an opaque AttributeError
backend/tests/test_chat_router.py still passes

stories.title: ResearchLoading indicator renders under every prior user message, not just the in-flight one
stories.description: frontend/src/pages/chat/component/chat-message.tsx:86-95 - status computed per-item as loading?'processing':'success' and rendered under every ChatRole.User bubble whenever deepResearch/useDeep is on.
acceptanceCriteria: The ResearchLoading indicator only renders under the last user message (or otherwise only reflects the actually in-flight request), not under every historical user message
npm run build succeeds
npm run lint shows no new issues vs baseline

stories.title: Markdown rendering disables GFM, breaking tables in finance answers
stories.description: frontend/src/components/markdown/index.tsx:21-23 - marked.parse(..., { gfm: false }) disables GitHub-flavored markdown (tables etc).
acceptanceCriteria: gfm is enabled (true) for markdown rendering unless there is a documented reason not to
A markdown string containing a table renders as an actual table element, not raw pipe text
npm run build succeeds

stories.title: history_rt empty session_id causes false-success no-ops
stories.description: backend/app/router/history_rt.py delete_session/get_messages: empty session_id passes Query(...) validation but _validate_session_id('') returns None, causing delete_session to report success while deleting nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: delete_session and get_messages reject/handle empty or invalid session_id consistently with chat()'s existing 400 behavior instead of silently no-oping
A new test confirms delete_session with an empty session_id returns an error rather than a false-success message
backend/tests/test_chat_router.py (or a new history router test file) passes

stories.title: es_client loopback detection uses substring match instead of exact host match
stories.description: backend/app/utils/es_client.py:5-9 _is_loopback uses `any(host in url for host in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS)`, a substring test vulnerable to lookalike hostnames.
acceptanceCriteria: Loopback detection parses the URL and compares the exact hostname against the loopback list rather than doing substring matching
Existing ES client behavior for real localhost/127.0.0.1 URLs is unchanged
backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py / test_chat_router.py still pass

stories.description: backend/app/service/web_search/web_search.py serper_images/serper_videos and backend/app/database/knowledgebase_operations.py verify_user_knowledgebase/get_user_kb_files have zero call sites.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirmed via grep that serper_images, serper_videos, verify_user_knowledgebase, get_user_kb_files have no callers anywhere in app/, scripts/, tests/
Those functions are removed (or, if kept intentionally, documented with a comment explaining why)
backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py and test_chat_router.py still pass

stories.title: process_actions dedup set resets per call, allowing duplicate memory entries across reflection iterations
stories.description: backend/app/service/agent/agent.py:469-494,684-709 - the seen dedup set is recreated on every process_actions call rather than persisting across reflection iterations.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate supplementary actions (e.g. the same finance_query re-issued in a later reflection iteration) are not appended to memory a second time
backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py still passes, and a new/updated test demonstrates the dedup persists across iterations

stories.title: _embed silently drops trailing chunks on embedding count mismatch
stories.description: backend/app/service/core/file_parse.py:76-95,176-186 - no assertion that len(vectors) == len(items); zip() silently truncates on mismatch and the file is still marked success.
acceptanceCriteria: A length mismatch between requested items and returned vectors is detected and raises (or returns an explicit failure) rather than silently truncating via zip
backend/tests/test_agent_loop.py / test_chat_router.py (or a new file_parse test) covers the mismatch case and passes

stories.title: index_finance.py never checks bulk-index result, same class as previously-fixed file_parse.py issue
stories.description: scripts/index_finance.py:256-259 - es.bulk(...) per-item errors are discarded while `written` is incremented unconditionally beforehand.
acceptanceCriteria: The bulk response's per-item errors are inspected and `written` (or an equivalent success count) reflects actual indexing success, not attempted count
Script still runs correctly against a normal successful indexing batch (smoke-checked or unit tested if feasible)

stories.title: index_finance.py inconsistent encoding handling across content types
stories.description: scripts/index_finance.py:278 vs :307,330 - filings use errors='ignore' but news/educational content use plain utf-8 read_text, which can raise UnicodeDecodeError and abort the whole run.
acceptanceCriteria: All three read paths (filings, news, educational) apply the same defensive encoding handling (errors='ignore' or find_codec)
A non-UTF-8 file no longer aborts the entire indexing run

stories.title: file_parse.py doc_id hash collision causes duplicate-content chunks to silently overwrite each other in ES
stories.description: backend/app/service/core/file_parse.py:189 - doc_id hash includes chunk text; two chunks with identical content collide and the later bulk op overwrites the earlier one.
acceptanceCriteria: doc_id incorporates a per-chunk ordinal (or other uniqueness guarantee) so identical-content chunks no longer collide and overwrite each other
backend/tests/test_chat_router.py / test_agent_loop.py still pass, and a new test confirms two identical-content chunks both get indexed with distinct ids

acceptanceCriteria: On api.session.create() rejection, sessionPromiseRef.current is cleared so a subsequent call retries instead of reusing a permanently-rejected promise

stories.title: useSendMessage/hot-questions have no error handling around session creation, risking undefined session_id navigation
stories.description: frontend/src/utils/useSendMessage.ts:11-18, frontend/src/components/hot-questions/index.tsx:20-24, frontend/src/pages/index/index.tsx:33 - no try/catch around session.create(), no guard against navigating with an undefined session_id.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigation to /chat/:sessionId is guarded so it never occurs with an undefined/falsy session_id
The session-creation call sites explicitly handle rejection (not just relying on the global error-toast plugin) so callers don't proceed as if a session_id exists
npm run build succeeds
